title: The 6 Best Neighborhoods in Charlotte for Every Lifestyle
summary: Compare Charlotte's top neighborhoods for every lifestyle, from walkable urban districts to family-friendly communities.

**Charlotte Neighborhoods: Quick Facts**


**6 Best Neighborhoods in Charlotte**


**1. Dilworth: Best Overall Neighborhood**


**2. South End: Best Neighborhood for Young Professionals**


**3. Ballantyne: Best Neighborhood for Families**


**4. SouthPark: Best Neighborhood for Retirees**


**5. Myers Park: Nicest Neighborhood in Charlotte**


**6. Plaza Midwood: Coolest Neighborhood in Charlotte**


**Finding the Right Charlotte Neighborhood for You**


Thanks to a growing job market, relatively moderate cost of living, and a wide range of housing options, Charlotte, NC, has become one of the[fastest-growing cities in the Southeast](https://www.wcnc.com/article/news/local/charlotte-population-growth-largest-us-cities/275-6ef7c772-b280-4a1d-a691-3004728761be) . With a metro area encompassing more than 3,000 square miles, there are literally hundreds of Charlotte neighborhoods to choose from. ​


From walkable districts near Uptown to established residential communities, there’s something for everyone in Charlotte, whether you’re a young professional, have a growing family, or recently retired. This guide explores some of the best neighborhoods in Charlotte based on housing costs, commute times, local amenities, and overall quality of life.


## Charlotte Neighborhoods: Quick Facts


Before we explore the details of the best neighborhoods in Charlotte, let’s take a quick look at the city’s overall housing market.


- Charlotte has more than 190 recognized neighborhoods spread across the city.
- The typical home value in Charlotte is approximately[$400,000](https://www.zillow.com/home-values/24043/charlotte-nc/) .
- The average rent in Charlotte is about[$1,995 per month](https://www.zillow.com/rental-manager/market-trends/charlotte-nc/) , though costs vary widely by neighborhood and size of house or apartment.
- Over[900,000 people](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/charlottecitynorthcarolina/PST045225) call Charlotte home, making it the 14th largest city in the United States and the largest city in North Carolina.
- Uptown Charlotte serves as the[city’s central business district](https://uptowncharlotte.com/business) and is home to the headquarters of Bank of America, Duke Energy, and Honeywell.
- The[LYNX Blue Line light rail](https://www.charlottenc.gov/CATS/Ride/Rail/Rail-Routes-and-Schedules) connects several popular Charlotte neighborhoods, including South End, NoDa, and University City.


## 6 Best Neighborhoods in Charlotte


You’ll find a variety of lifestyles in the many Charlotte neighborhoods, from walkable districts near Uptown to established residential communities farther from the city center. Some are known for their nightlife or being home to some of the best restaurants in Charlotte, while others attract residents with large homes, green parks, and top-rated schools.


The six neighborhoods below rank among the best neighborhoods in Charlotte. Our list includes the best neighborhoods for families, young professionals, retirees, and those looking for luxury living in the Southeast.


### 1. Dilworth: Best Overall Neighborhood


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-couple-spending-time-together-by-the-lake-9652795/)


- **Median Home Sale Price:**[$797,000](https://www.redfin.com/neighborhood/127806/NC/Charlotte/Dilworth/housing-market)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$2,004](https://www.apartments.com/dilworth-charlotte-nc/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 5–10 minutes
- **Vibe:** Walkable, historic, established


Dilworth is one of the best Charlotte neighborhoods for residents who want beautiful tree-lined streets and historic character without giving up easy access to Uptown. Developed in the late 1800s as[Charlotte’s first streetcar suburb](https://dilworthcenter.org/dilworth-charlotte-a-historic-neighborhoods-story-and-community-legacy/) , the neighborhood features a mix of renovated bungalows, townhomes, apartments, and local businesses.


​Dilworth centers around[East Boulevard](https://www.axios.com/local/charlotte/2016/06/09/east-boulevard-charlottes-restaurant-row-53392) , where residents enjoy restaurants, coffee shops, and shopping at boutiques. Dilworth is also home to[Freedom Park](https://www.charlottesgotalot.com/things-to-do/outdoors-adventure/freedom-park) , one of Charlotte’s most popular public spaces. You’ll find walking trails, athletic fields, playgrounds, and a seven-acre lake, as well as events like the annual[Festival in the Park](https://festivalinthepark.org/) . The neighborhood’s central location, strong housing market, and walkability make Dilworth one of the best places to live in Charlotte overall.


### 2. South End: Best Neighborhood for Young Professionals


- **Median Home Sale Price:**[$765,000](https://www.redfin.com/neighborhood/30383/NC/Charlotte/South-End/housing-market)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$1,991](https://www.apartments.com/south-end-charlotte-nc/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 5 minutes
- **Vibe:** Social, convenient, modern


South End is widely considered one of the best neighborhoods in Charlotte, NC, for young professionals. Located just south of Uptown, the neighborhood is comprised of a mix of apartments, townhomes, offices, restaurants, breweries, and retail spaces. It’s connected to other parts of the city by the LYNX Blue Line and the[Charlotte Rail Trail](https://www.charlotterailtrail.org/) .


Many residents choose South End for its walkability, with easy access to popular destinations including[Atherton Mill](https://athertonsouthend.com/) ,[Club West Brewing](https://www.clubwestbrew.com/) , and the[Charlotte Beer Garden](https://charlottebeergarden.com/) . As part of the Rail Trail, the area sees various community events throughout the year, including Front Porch Sundays and First Friday Gallery Crawl. If you’re looking for a quick commute to work and easy access to dining and entertainment, look no further than South End, one of the coolest neighborhoods in Charlotte.


### 3. Ballantyne: Best Neighborhood for Families


- **Median Home Sale Price:**[$682,000](https://www.redfin.com/neighborhood/378088/NC/Charlotte/Ballantyne-East/housing-market) (East) and[$523,000](https://www.redfin.com/neighborhood/380689/NC/Charlotte/Ballantyne-West/housing-market) (West)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$1,601](https://www.apartments.com/ballantyne-charlotte-nc/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 25–30 minutes
- **Vibe:** Family-oriented, suburban, polished


Families often flock to suburbs and, when it comes to the upscale suburbs of Charlotte, it’s Davidson and Weddington that usually come to mind. However, if you’re looking to enjoy upscale suburban amenities without leaving the city limits, then Ballantyne is the place for you.


​Residents have easy access to destinations such as[The Bowl at Ballantyne](https://thebowlnc.com/) , a mixed-use district with restaurants, entertainment, and community events, as well as the[Ballantyne Country Club](https://ballantyneclub.com/) and nearby[Four Mile Creek Greenway](https://www.matthewsnc.gov/pview.aspx?id=20988&catid=0) .


Ballantyne is often ranked among the best neighborhoods in Charlotte, NC, for families, thanks to its[newer housing developments](https://www.listregroup.com/ballantyne-reimagined-the-future-of-luxury-living-in-south-charlotte) ,[highly rated schools](https://www.niche.com/k12/search/best-schools/n/ballantyne-west-charlotte-nc/) , and abundance of parks and recreational facilities. Located in south Charlotte, the area offers larger homes and master-planned communities that appeal to families looking for space.


### 4. SouthPark: Best Neighborhood for Retirees


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/photo-of-house-facade-12127809/)


- **Median Home Sale Price:**[$705,000](https://www.redfin.com/neighborhood/548755/NC/Charlotte/Southpark/housing-market)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$1,585](https://www.apartments.com/south-park-charlotte-nc/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 15-20 minutes
- **Vibe:** Convenient, comfortable, established


SouthPark is one of the best neighborhoods in Charlotte, NC, for retirees due to its central location and convenient access to shopping, dining, and health care services. SouthPark offers a mix of single-family homes, condos, and luxury apartments, and is anchored by[SouthPark Mall](https://www.simon.com/mall/southpark) , one of the premier shopping destinations in the Carolinas.


​Residents appreciate the area’s mature tree canopy, well-maintained neighborhoods, and easy access to everyday amenities. If you’re looking to stay active while enjoying a quieter pace of life, look no further than SouthPark.


### 5. Myers Park: Nicest Neighborhood in Charlotte


- **Median Home Sale Price:**[$1.5 million](https://www.redfin.com/neighborhood/53363/NC/Charlotte/Myers-Park/housing-market)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$1,579](https://www.apartments.com/myers-park-charlotte-nc/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 10 minutes
- **Vibe:** Historic, upscale, residential


What is the nicest neighborhood in Charlotte? Many locals point to Myers Park. Known for its stately homes, oak-lined streets, and[historic architecture](https://www.axios.com/local/charlotte/2019/05/14/most-beautiful-homes-in-myers-park-according-to-architect-and-professor-garrett-nelson-164929) , Myers Park has long been one of the nicest neighborhoods in Charlotte. The area is also regularly mentioned among the richest neighborhoods in Charlotte due to the high property values and large estates.


Myers Park sits just south of Uptown and is home to several Charlotte landmarks, including[Queens University](https://www.queens.edu/) and portions of the[Little Sugar Creek Greenway](https://www.traillink.com/trail/little-sugar-creek-greenway/) . While housing costs are among the highest in the city, residents gain access to a highly sought-after location and some of Charlotte’s most recognizable homes.


### 6. Plaza Midwood: Coolest Neighborhood in Charlotte


Free image via[Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/friendly-barista-serving-customer-in-cafe-36729745/)


- **Median Home Sale Price:**[$986,000](https://www.redfin.com/neighborhood/51086/NC/Charlotte/Plaza-Midwood/housing-market)
- **Average Monthly Rent:**[$1,532](https://www.apartments.com/plaza-midwood-charlotte-nc/)
- **Commute to Downtown:** 10 minutes
- **Vibe:** Creative, eclectic, local


Plaza Midwood is often considered one of the coolest neighborhoods in Charlotte thanks to its variety of independent businesses, locally owned restaurants, and active arts scene. Located just east of Uptown, the neighborhood features a mix of historic homes and renovated bungalows and apartments, as well as newer infill development.


​Residents spend weekends exploring local favorites such as[Midwood Park](https://www.charlottesgotalot.com/things-to-do/outdoors-adventure/midwood-park) ,[The Common Market](https://commonmarketisgood.com/) , and the neighborhood’s collection of[restaurants](https://www.opentable.com/features/best-casual-restaurants-plaza-midwood-nc) , coffee shops, and boutiques. Plaza Midwood offers a distinctly local feel that sets it apart from many newer developments in Charlotte. It’s one of the best places to live in Charlotte for residents who value walkability and neighborhood character.


## Finding the Right Charlotte Neighborhood for You


Whether you’re interested in a walkable neighborhood close to the best things to do in Charlotte, or you’re looking for a quiet residential community with good schools, comparing your options ahead of time can help you find the right fit before moving to Charlotte.
